recommendation.summary: dsh-tui 0.12.0 is an interactive terminal UI plugin for DeepSeek Harness, mounted as a Cordis bundle patch over dsh-base. Author intent is a single TUI plane: the README documents `dsh-tui` / `dst` and states `dsh-tui` and `dsh --profile dsh-tui` are equivalent, so the evidenced installation profile is `dsh-tui`. Node: engines.node is `^22.19 || >=24` in both source and published manifests (declared support for 22 and 24), while the README states CI uses Node 24 and the CI workflow pins node-version 24 — so 24 is the strongest author-intent signal (ci-tested) and 22 is a declared-support baseline. Development package manager is pnpm@11.21.0 from the source manifest; no profile-scoped package manager or override is evidenced, and the workspace overrides in pnpm-workspace.yaml are development-only and must not be transferred to a consumer profile. Author DSH baseline: the primary validated line is 0.2.0-rc.2 (pnpm-workspace.yaml comment plus README compatibility statement), matching the target DSH version. No headless, SDK, or ACP workflow is documented, so only tui is selected. This recommendation records author intent from repository evidence; it does not prove compatibility.

conclusion.statement: dsh-tui 0.12.0 (@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui) was reviewed and exercised against DSH 0.2.0-rc.2 on the two Node majors evidenced by the repository: 22 (engines.node ^22.19 || >=24, declared support) and 24 (README states CI uses Node 24; ci.yml pins node-version 24). Native plane: both dsh-tui-node22 and dsh-tui-node24 are compatible — the exact artifact installed, registered, loaded, and satisfied its direct Node peer contracts (artifact sha256 bb23c50f...a178). TUI plane: both dsh-tui-node22-tui and dsh-tui-node24-tui reached the surface and passed runtime, artifact, profile (dsh plugin add created the custom dsh-tui profile), install, registration, host, surface and interaction stages, but are surface-incompatible because the TUI produced a frame and did not stop after the bounded shutdown input. This is a shutdown/exit-path observation on the interactive TUI plane, not a load or install failure, and it is identical on both Node majors. No adapter (SDK/ACP) cells were scheduled, matching the review finding that the plugin documents no SDK or ACP workflow. The recommendation recorded author intent only and does not prove compatibility; accepted native cells mean the report was recorded, not that the plugin is compatible.
